title: What do the diagonals do in a rectangle with equal sides?
description: A square with sides of five centimetres is drawn with both diagonals, and the eight angles and the two diagonal lengths are measured. Keeko's doubt is that only a square has equal diagonals, and the video breaks it.
teaching_notes: One idea: in a square all eight angles made by the diagonals and the sides are forty five degrees, and the two diagonals are equal. Watch for students who think equal diagonals belong only to a square.

source: In your experiment, consider the case when all four sides of
video_script.why: A learner measures the angles and the diagonals of a square and sees that all eight angles are alike and the two diagonals are equal.
video_script.substitution: the book's rectangle PQRS with all four sides equal, drawn with sides of five centimetres
video_script.anchor: the square PQRS of the book with both its diagonals drawn
video_script.wrong_answer: only a square has equal diagonals
video_script.wrong_move: thinks equal diagonals are special to a square and ignores that every rectangle has them
video_script.payoff_line: In a square all eight angles are forty five degrees, and the two diagonals are equal.

final_answer.value: all eight angles are 45 degrees; the two diagonals are equal, about 7.1 cm for a 5 cm square
final_answer.spoken: all the angles are forty five degrees and the two diagonals are equal, about seven point one centimetres for a square of five centimetres

maths_rules: each corner of the square is 90 degrees and the diagonal cuts it in two equal parts: 90 / 2 = 45
the eight angles made by the diagonals and the sides are each 45 degrees
the diagonal of a square of side 5 cm is 5 x 1.414 = about 7.07, so about 7.1 cm
the two diagonals of a square are equal, and every rectangle has two equal diagonals
